data.narrative:
Radian Aerospace is a Seed-stage space & aerospace company that has raised $27.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private equivalents including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs, though narrow-stage peer multiples were insufficient for reliable triangulation.

Of three methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using total capital raised ($27.5M) as a baseline proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to next stage yields an implied valuation of $69M. Public-comp anchoring could not proceed absent disclosed revenue; the Space & Aerospace sector median P/S stands at 23.9x across six public tickers, but target revenue is not on file. Peer-median analysis was likewise inapplicable: while 11 same-sector peers exist, zero met the narrow filters of identical or adjacent stage and similar valuation tier required for statistical reliability.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $58M to $79M, centered on $69M. Key uncertainties include the absence of financial metrics (revenue, burn rate, unit economics) typical of private disclosure, limited fungibility between pre-revenue aerospace ventures, and the stage-progression method's inherent reliance on historical norms rather than company-specific fundamentals. Refinement would require revenue guidance or comparable transaction data at identical development stage.
